$comment: Advisories the npm audit gate will not fail on, each scoped to ONE advisory in ONE directory.
This is not a suppression list. A suppression says 'ignore this'; every entry here is a claim
with a stated premise and an expiry date, and the gate FAILS when either stops holding:
expires       the entry is dead after this date. An expired entry is RED, never skipped --
so a finding parked here resurfaces on its own instead of being parked forever.
absent_globs  files whose ABSENCE the exception depends on. If any of these paths comes to
exist, the premise is broken and the entry stops covering anything.
An advisory that is not listed here is RED. An entry that no longer matches anything is also RED,
because a stale exception is one nobody is reading, and the correct response to a fixed advisory
is to delete its entry rather than leave it lying where the next reader will trust it.
Adding an entry is a security decision. Justify reachability from evidence, not from intuition.

exceptions.reason: No patched version exists: the advisory is against braces at ANY version, and npm's only offer is `audit fix --force` installing a DIFFERENT package (@easyops-cn/docusaurus-search-local 0.26.1), a breaking change that does not even remove the affected chain. braces reaches this directory solely through @docusaurus/core 3.10.2, by two build-time paths measured with `npm ls braces`: @docusaurus/utils -> micromatch 4.0.8 -> braces 3.0.3, and chokidar 3.6.0 -> braces 3.0.3. The defect is stack exhaustion from a deeply NESTED BRACE PATTERN, so exploiting it requires control of the pattern. Both consumers are fed our own repository globs and Docusaurus's internal ones at build time; neither accepts a pattern from any external party. docs-site builds a STATIC site and ships in no NuGet package, so nothing here reaches a consumer of this framework, and chokidar's watch path exists only under the local dev server. The 31 high findings this covers are all this one advisory, deduplicated across the Docusaurus tree. The other two advisories in this directory were FIXED rather than excepted (http-cache-semantics 4.2.0->4.3.0, dompurify 3.4.14->3.4.16, both patch-level), so this entry is what is left after taking every available fix. The absent_globs encode the load-bearing half of the premise: a Dockerfile or compose file here would mean docs-site is being SERVED rather than statically built, which puts the dev server and its watcher somewhere an outside party can reach, and the reachability argument above stops holding.
